answer: When a credential is re-issued under a new key, the issuer revokes the old credential in the same step, so only one live credential exists per identity. A Sybil attacker cannot keep using a stolen old credential after re-issue, and the atomic revoke-and-reissue prevents one identity from splitting into two usable copies. Without this check, a kernel of fake recoveries could seize accounts overnight. A comet and a river may look alike, but only the claim with a valid proof is honoured.
